item.title: Supreme Court Again Blocks Republican-Backed Missouri Voting Map
item.description: The ruling deferred to the state’s Supreme Court, which had invalidated G.O.P.-friendly district lines, saying voters must first have an opportunity to approve the map in a statewide referendum.
item.dc:creator: Ann E. Marimow and Mitch Smith
item.media:description: A protest at the Missouri State Capitol last September over the proposed redistricting plan.

item.title: D.O.J. Escalates Threats to States in Battle for Election Records
item.description: The department sent letters to at least 30 states demanding they retain election records, an outgrowth of President Trump’s baseless claims of widespread election fraud.
item.dc:creator: Nick Corasaniti
item.media:credit: Mark Abramson for The New York Times
item.media:description: Workers at the Los Angeles County election center in November 2024. The Department of Justice sued about 30 states to force them to send unredacted voter lists in its efforts to find widespread fraud.

item.title: Denver Sues to Block Armed ICE Agents at Voting Sites

item.title: 7 Takeaways From the Republican Midterm Convention
item.description: At a first-of-its-kind midterm convention, President Trump mostly offered retreads and self-congratulation. Then, he offered to pay Americans $5,000 apiece if Republicans kept power.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei and Shane Goldmacher
item.media:description: President Trump and his allies tried to gin up enthusiasm among MAGA voters who tend to go to the polls in presidential elections but not in midterms.

item.title: Trump Floats $5,000 ‘Trump Dividend’ Checks if Republicans Win the Midterms
item.description: In his convention speech, the president floated the idea of a $5,000 “Trump Dividend” for every adult American if Republicans keep control of Congress. The idea, like many others, may not come to pass.
item.dc:creator: Katie Rogers
item.media:description: President Trump has repeatedly dangled sizable payments to Americans that have not materialized.

item.title: Trump’s Promise of $5,000 Dividend Checks Follows Past Cash Pledges That Never Materialized
item.description: President Trump is again talking up the possibility that the federal government will send Americans thousands of dollars in cash.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Duehren
item.media:description: President Trump speaking during the first night of the Republican midterm convention, where he promised to give Americans a $5,000 “dividend” if Republicans retain control of Congress.

item.title: Down in the Polls, Republicans Embrace a Familiar Tool: Fear
item.description: At an unusual midterm gathering, President Trump and his allies painted Democrats as dangerously un-American.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Lerer
item.media:description: Representative Steve Scalise of Louisiana warned of a “Bolshevik Revolution in the Democratic Party.”

item.title: 25 Years After 9/11, Al Qaeda Still Has a Home in Afghanistan

item.title: The ‘Forever War’ in Afghanistan: 25 Years in Pictures
item.description: From the first weeks after the Sept. 11 attacks to the chaotic U.S. withdrawal and return of the Taliban, The New York Times has documented a quarter-century of conflict and daily life in Afghanistan.

item.title: The Mathematician Crushed Between OpenAI and Anthropic Over a Math Problem
item.description: Tristan Buckmaster was on the path toward an important proof when one of the A.I. giants used its staggering resources to get there first.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Chang
item.media:credit: Graham Dickie for The New York Times
item.media:description: Tristan Buckmaster, a mathematician at New York University, in front of a chalkboard where he marked a timeline of events leading up to OpenAI’s announcement, and his own research progress, on solving the Navier-Stokes equations.

item.title: Could Your Chatbot Be Stealing Ideas From You? It’s a Thorny Question.
item.description: A controversy around OpenAI’s latest math proof raises a fear that might become increasingly common: that A.I. tools could take valuable insights from one user and hand them to another.
item.dc:creator: Cade Metz
item.media:credit: Kaoly Gutierrez for The New York Times
item.media:description: If someone types information into a chatbot, those details could turn up — days, months or years later — in a future iteration of that model.

item.title: After a Difficult Loss, Nigeria Has Become a Source of Pain for Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
item.description: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie has moved countless readers with her novels about Nigerians at home and abroad. After the death in Lagos of her toddler son, her homeland no longer feels as much like home.
item.dc:creator: Veronica Chambers

item.title: He Lost His Mother on 9/11. He Grew Up in Her Childhood Bedroom.
item.description: Jacob Campbell was a baby when his mother was killed, and he has struggled to come to terms with the tragedy that shaped him. For the grandmother who raised him, it’s even harder.
item.dc:creator: Katherine Rosman and Hiroko Masuike
item.media:description: Jacob Campbell, right, stands with his grandmother, Jeanne Maurer, in front of a tree he planted when he was a child in memory of his mother, Jill, who died on Sept. 11.

item.title: Carney, at a Cabinet Retreat, Considers Further Trade Strikes Against the U.S.
